reason: The provided sources robustly support a compelling 45-second story with 18 multi-sourced claims from independent websites.
story: At the outermost border of our Solar System lies the Oort cloud, a giant theoretical shell of icy bodies surrounding the Sun. First postulated by Ernst Öpik in 1932 and expanded by Jan Oort in 1950, this frozen reservoir sits between 2,000 and 100,000 astronomical units away, extending up to a quarter of the distance to the nearest star. Formed 4.6 billion years ago when young giant planets flung leftover planetesimals into deep space, these icy worlds are nudged inward by galactic tides and passing stars to become long-period comets. Because no telescope has ever directly observed the Oort cloud, it remains unseen. NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft, traveling a million miles a day, will take about 300 years just to reach its inner edge and roughly 30,000 years to pass through it completely. Long before it arrives, its power supply will fail, leaving humanity to study this frozen frontier through cosmic driftwood.
angle: NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft will take 300 years just to reach the inner edge of the Oort cloud and 30,000 years to pass through it, yet its power source will die long before arrival.

claims.claim: Dutch astronomer Jan Oort proposed the existence of a vast comet cloud in 1950.
Estonian astronomer Ernst Öpik first proposed a reservoir of long-period comets at the edge of the Solar System in 1932.
The Oort cloud is a theoretical, roughly spherical shell of icy bodies surrounding the Solar System.
The inner edge of the Oort cloud is estimated to begin between 2,000 and 5,000 astronomical units from the Sun.
The outer boundary of the Oort cloud extends up to 100,000 astronomical units from the Sun.
The outer reaches of the Oort cloud extend roughly a quarter to halfway to the nearest star.
The Oort cloud serves as the primary reservoir for long-period comets entering the inner Solar System.
Objects in the Oort cloud formed closer to the Sun and were flung outward by young giant planets 4.6 billion years ago.
Tidal forces from the Milky Way galaxy help alter the orbits of Oort cloud objects and direct them inward toward the Sun.
Gravitational nudges from passing stars can disturb Oort cloud objects and send them toward the inner Solar System.
NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft will take approximately 300 years to reach the inner edge of the Oort cloud.
It will take Voyager 1 roughly 30,000 years to completely pass through the Oort cloud.
Voyager 1 will run out of power and cease operating scientific instruments long before reaching the Oort cloud.
The Oort cloud has never been directly observed by any telescope.
The Oort cloud is divided into an outer spherical region and an inner disc-shaped region called the Hills cloud.
The dwarf planet Sedna is associated with the inner region of the Oort cloud.
Halley-family comets originally originated in the Oort cloud before being captured into smaller orbits.
Oort cloud objects are mostly composed of volatile ices like water, methane, ethane, carbon monoxide, and hydrogen cyanide.

disputed: The exact outer boundary distance varies between sources (ranging from 50,000 AU up to 200,000 AU); a script should state it extends up to 100,000 AU or state 'estimates range up to 200,000 AU'.

Hypotheses regarding undetected companion bodies like Nemesis or Tyche driving comet showers have been disproved or lack supporting evidence; leave these out or present them strictly as past debunked hypotheses.
